pg007_n0008: Sport Studies play an important role in student’s physical, mental and social development.
pg007_n0009: In Sport Studies, students are provided with the opportunities to participate in a variety of physical activities including sports and games for leisure and competition purposes.
pg007_n0010: In this chapter, you will learn the concept and elements of Sport Studies, categories and functions of sports, importance of studying Sport Studies and its relationship with other disciplines.
pg007_n0011: The competencies developed will enable you to appreciate the values of sports and develop interest of participating in various sports activities.
pg007_n0019: In this book, the term Sport Studies is used synonymously with Physical Education, P E.
pg007_n0020: Sport Studies is the study of sports and the associated human movements.
pg007_n0021: It refers to an academic discipline that provides a platform for cognitive and motor skills, character and behavioural development for individual well-being and social changes through physical activities and sports.
pg007_n0022: Sport Studies subject aims to develop students’ physical competence, sport skills, knowledge of movement, safety skills, and its applications in performing a wide range of activities associated with sports and healthy lifestyle.
pg007_n0023: Thus, the subject remains a vital part of the total process of education that promotes active lifestyles and enables individual to participate in lifelong sports, exercise and recreational activities during leisure time.
pg009_n0005: Sport Studies subject uses different elements which overlap in school programmes to achieve the goal.
pg009_n0006: The major vehicle of sport studies is physical activity.
pg009_n0010: A physical activity is any bodily movement that requires energy expenditure.
pg009_n0011: Any motion you do throughout the day is considered physical activity.
pg009_n0012: For example, cooking, taking shower, walking, carrying chairs, and even speaking can be considered as physical activities.
pg009_n0013: A physical activity involves sport related and non-sport related activities.
pg009_n0014: In the sport related category physical activities includes sports, exercise, dance, games and play.
pg009_n0018: Plays are commonly played by children.
pg009_n0019: A play can involve both physical and mental engagement and is often characterised by spontaneity and creativity.
pg009_n0020: Play activities may or may not be planned and can take place anywhere, open spaces, sandpits or recreation rooms, and starting any time.
pg009_n0021: Sport Studies incorporate elements of play to make the learning process more enjoyable and effective.
pg009_n0025: Games are structured activities that involve interaction and competition among participants.
pg009_n0026: They can be played for recreational purposes or as part of a competitive sport.
pg009_n0027: Games often involve setting objectives and rules confined to that particular context that players must follow to achieve the goals of the game.
pg009_n0028: Games can be used in sport studies classes to foster skills learning, knowledge acquisition, character and behaviour development.
pg009_n0032: Sports are organised activities that require physical exertion and skills in which an individual or team compete against another.
pg009_n0033: Sports are considered as highly organised, formalised and competitive form of play.
pg009_n0034: Sport usually have institutionalised rules and regulations, and participants compete against one another or in teams to accomplish a goal, such as winning a game or a match.
pg009_n0035: Examples of sports are football, basketball, swimming, netball, and athletics, track and field events.
pg009_n0039: Exercise is a planned, structured, and repetitive body movement.
pg009_n0040: Exercise is used to maintain and increase physical fitness, improve health and enhance sport skills.
pg012_n0005: Team sports are competitive physical activities in which individuals work together in groups as a team to achieve a common goal, as shown in Figure one point three.
pg012_n0006: For example, football, netball, volleyball, field hockey, cricket and a swimming relay.

pg013_n0005: Entertainment: Sports are perceived as a source of amusement where individuals derive pleasure and alleviate stress by either engaging in or observing sporting events;
pg013_n0008: Through sports people can learn various aspects which are useful in daily life such as:
pg013_n0012: Focus: Engaging in sports improves your ability to concentrate on the present moment, leaving the past behind as insignificant and the future as uncertain;
pg013_n0015: Valuing the process: Engaging in sports instills the valuable lesson of prioritising the process over the outcome. When the process is handled with diligence, achievement and success naturally follow;
pg013_n0019: Tolerance: Sports instill in you the value of tolerance.
pg013_n0020: It emphasises that success may be right around the corner, and with persistence any goal is attainable.
pg013_n0021: When you decide to give up, you never truly realise how close you might be to achieving success;
pg013_n0025: Leadership skills: Leading diverse individuals from various backgrounds towards a shared purpose or aim; and
pg013_n0029: Team work: Collaborating within a team with a shared objective, placing others before oneself, and setting aside personal differences.
pg013_n0032: Source of income: Sports have evolved into an international business, offering diverse economic prospects to numerous individuals in society, especially the younger generation. Engaging in sports enables people to find employment opportunities as coaches, educators, referees, administrators, legal experts, analysts, agents and athletes;
pg013_n0036: Rehabilitation: Engaging in sports can serve as a means to enhance the overall physical, mental, and psychological health of individuals.
pg013_n0037: For example, sports programmes are designed to aid the recovery of people having physical and mental disorders; and
pg013_n0041: Cultural transmission: Sports can serve as a means of passing societal culture from one generation to the next.
pg013_n0042: For example, during football matches, spectators display their cultural identity by wearing traditional attire, singing traditional songs, and conveying important messages that can be adopted by younger generations.

pg015_n0004: On the other side, sports participants promote body health and fitness.
pg015_n0005: Thus, by considering that relationship, Sport studies educators can tailor fitness programmes for optimal physical well-being and performance in sports.
pg015_n0009: The relationship between Sport Studies and Physics is significant as they share knowledge on biomechanics and kinesiology.
pg015_n0010: Sport Studies subject primarily focuses on physical fitness, sports, and movement.
pg015_n0011: The subject inherently involves principles and laws of motion, force, energy, density, floatation and machines.
pg015_n0012: Understanding the physics behind body mechanics and sports performance can enhance learning and improve athletes’ performance.
pg015_n0016: The relationship between Sport Studies and Chemistry exists through the understanding of biochemistry and nutrition.
pg015_n0017: Chemistry plays a crucial role in studying the chemical processes that occur within the body during exercise, metabolism, and energy production.
pg015_n0018: Knowledge of Chemistry helps in developing dietary recommendations, understanding the effects of various substances, like supplements or drugs, on physical performance, and optimising training regimens for better outcomes in Sport Studies.
pg015_n0022: The connection between Sport Studies and Mathematics exists in various aspects of sports and exercises.
pg015_n0023: Mathematics is used to analyse and interpret data related to fitness levels, performance metrics, and biomechanics.
pg015_n0024: Additionally, mathematical concepts like geometry, statistics, and calculus can be applied to understand motion, trajectories, and optimal training strategies.
pg015_n0025: Integrating Mathematics into Sport Studies can lead to more informed decisions, improved training methods, and better overall physical performance.
pg015_n0029: The relationship between Sport Studies and Geography is evident in the context of outdoor physical activities.
pg015_n0030: Geographical knowledge, skills and features influence participant’s choice of sports and recreational activities.
pg015_n0031: Understanding geographical factors like altitude, temperature, and landscapes is essential for planning and organising sport studies programmes.
pg015_n0032: For example, some sports like orienteering require understanding of map reading, grid, weather, altitude and wild life.
pg016_n0005: The connection between Sport Studies and History can be seen through the evolution of sports and physical activities over time.
pg016_n0006: Historical records reveal how sports and exercise have been an integral part of human civilisations, serving roles in recreation, warfare preparation, and cultural practices.
pg016_n0007: Studying the history of various sports provides insights into the development of sports, the impact of various cultures on physical activities, and the societal attitudes towards physical fitness and athleticism throughout different eras.
pg016_n0008: Understanding this historical context can enrich modern sport studies programmes and highlight the significance of physical activities in shaping societies across the ages.
pg016_n0012: The relationship between Sport Studies and Civic education lies in the ability to promote the values of teamwork, cooperation, and fair play.
pg016_n0013: Sport Studies subject provides a platform for students to engage in sports and physical activities, thus, fostering a sense of citizenship.
pg016_n0014: Through Sport Studies, students learn essential aspects of good citizenship including respect, sportsmanship, and inclusivity.
pg016_n0015: Moreover, sport studies can contribute to the overall well-being of individuals, thereby creating healthier and more active members of society, which is beneficial to the civic health of the community.
pg016_n0019: The Sport Studies and Languages, local and foreign, are related.
pg016_n0020: Sport Studies improve communication and language acquisition by improving cognitive abilities, concentration, interaction and teamwork.
pg016_n0021: Also, linguistic abilities can be used to follow instructions, game plans in sports, and work well with others while exercising or in sports activities.
pg016_n0025: There are several ways to observe the connection between Music and Sport Studies.
pg016_n0026: For example, including music into sport studies lessons might improve the overall learning environment.
pg016_n0027: Exercise programmes that incorporate music such as aerobic dance can make the activity more interesting and encourage students to move rhythmically, improve coordination and endurance.
pg016_n0028: Additionally, music can be utilised to set the mood for warm-ups, cool-downs, and various training phases, affecting the class’s pacing and excitement.
pg016_n0029: On the contrary, music composition and performance can be improved through exercises and sports, consequently stimulating individual's functions and performance.

pg018_n0008: When entering a sport ground, a court, or a track, keep in mind that safety is more than just a precaution.
pg018_n0009: Safety forms the basis for unforgettable sporting experiences.
pg018_n0010: In this chapter, you will learn the meaning of safety and its importance, sports injuries and their causes, as well as safety practices towards participants’ safety and successful performance.
pg018_n0011: The competencies developed will enhance your ability to perform various sports safely and ensure a responsible athletic attitude.
pg018_n0015: The effect of failure to observe safety in sports activities
pg018_n0019: In any physical exercise and sports, safety should be considered important in all aspects at all ages and levels of learning.
pg018_n0020: The beauty of sports and exercises can be affected by accidents and injuries.
pg018_n0021: It is therefore, important that everyone acquires safety skills to prevent unnecessary injuries in physical activities and sports.
pg018_n0029: Reduce the risk of injuries in physical activities;
pg019_n0008: Reduce the risk of infection and disease risks;
pg019_n0011: Enhance comfort and stress free; and
pg019_n0014: Develop a positive image of sports in the society.
pg019_n0018: In exercise and sporting activities, it is common to encounter circumstances which may cause injuries.
pg019_n0019: Injuries that occur immediately during the event are called acute injuries while those that develop slowly from many events are called overuse injuries.
pg019_n0020: For example, if you fall down and get cut by a piece of glass, the cut is considered acute injury.
pg019_n0021: If you have been playing every day without getting enough rest such that your knee is uncomfortable and start swelling, that is overuse injury.
pg019_n0022: Therefore, all injuries fall into these two groups, acute and overuse injuries.
pg019_n0024: There are various injuries that occur during exercises and sporting activities in muscles, joints, bones and blood vessels.
pg019_n0025: These injuries include blisters, bruises, dislocation, sprain, fracture, strain, skin cuts, abrasions, muscle cramp and nose bleeding.
pg019_n0029: Blister is an injury which occurs when the skin is frequently rubbed and causes fluid to fill a space between layers of skin, as shown in Figure two point one.
pg019_n0030: For example, foot blisters occur when an athlete wears un-fitting shoes.
pg019_n0031: A prolonged holding a tennis or badminton racket may cause blisters on the hand.
pg019_n0032: The punctured blister become more prone to infection, thus, care must be taken to keep it.

pg020_n0011: Bruises are common injuries in sports where, blood is trapped and leaks out to the skin as a result of a direct blow or fall.
pg020_n0012: The affected area may undergo swelling with reddish or purple mark on the skin, as shown in Figure two point two.
pg020_n0013: The common symptoms of bruises include, pain and tenderness, swelling, warmth or heat, stiffness or limited range of motion, and itching as it heals.

pg020_n0019: Joints can become dislocated when bones are forced out of their normal positions, as shown in Figure two point three.
pg020_n0020: This is a slip-out of bones in the joint which occurs when extreme force wrenches the ligament.
pg020_n0021: Dislocation occurs where the surrounding tissues like tendons and ligament are damaged.
pg020_n0022: The common symptoms of dislocation include, severe pain, deformity, swelling, limited range of motion, numbness or tingling, instability, difficulty in using the affected limb, popping sounds, shock and disorientation.
pg020_n0023: This injury needs medical treatment to relocate the joint.

pg021_n0009: Sprain is an overstretch or tearing of ligament that occurs when the joint is forced to move beyond its limit, as shown in Figure two point four.
pg021_n0010: It is a result of sudden or un expected wrenching movement of the joint.
pg021_n0011: This injury can be minor or quite serious.
pg021_n0012: Once ligament is ruptured, it requires extensive medical treatment.

pg022_n0005: A fracture is a crack or break of a bone.
pg022_n0006: When a fracture is open, it is called a compound fracture, and when it is closed it is called a simple fracture, which can be either a displaced or non-displaced fracture, as shown in Figure two point five.
pg022_n0007: The symptoms of a fracture may differ depending on its type and location.
pg022_n0008: However, the common symptoms include pain, swelling, bruise or discoloration of the skin around the fracture site, deformity or an abnormal appearance of the injured limb or area, limited range of motion, tenderness, numbness or tingling, crepitus, shock, and disorientation.

pg022_n0026: The signs and symptoms of strain can vary in severity depending on the extent of the injury, but common signs and symptoms include pain, swelling, tenderness, stiffness, instability, and decreased function.

pg025_n0005: When your friend gets injured during physical activities, you are required to give initial assistance to reduce the danger of the injury and promote healing.
pg025_n0006: The practice of giving help to an injured person is called first aiding.
pg025_n0007: The protocol of giving first aid is abbreviated as R I C E R.
pg025_n0008: This is a procedure used to handle various injuries immediately after they occur.
pg025_n0009: R I C E R helps to relieve pain, reduce swelling, and promote healing of the injury.
pg025_n0013: Stop any activity immediately and lie down in a safe place to ensure rest, stability, and support to an injured part of the body in a comfortable position to limit additional harm.
pg025_n0017: Icing is the application of a cold pack or an ice pack around an injured area to reduce pain and slow the internal bleeding and swelling.
pg025_im001: A hand presses an ice pack on an injured ankle to help reduce pain and swelling.
pg025_n0023: Compression is the application of slight pressure to the injured area for a closed injury by using compression bandage, as shown in Figure two point ten.
pg025_n0024: For an open injury, compression is applied on the proximal side of the injury.
pg025_im002: A bandage is wrapped around an injured ankle to give gentle pressure and reduce swelling.

pg029_n0009: Fitness is an important element of body healthy and performance in various activities.
pg029_n0010: In the light of the contemporary emphasis on promoting lifetime wellness, physical fitness should become central in a mindset of every human being.
pg029_n0011: Having fitness skills helps people to improve their health, as well as enhancing performance.
pg029_n0012: In this chapter, you will learn the meaning, importance, attributes and components of mental and physical fitness.
pg029_n0013: The competencies developed will enable you to improve your health and perform well in sports and other activities involved.
pg029_n0017: Things which may help you to be fit in sports
pg029_n0021: Fitness is the person’s entire physical and mental well-being.
pg029_n0022: It is achieved by the combination of regular physical activity, a healthy diet, appropriate rest, and other healthy lifestyle choices.
pg029_n0023: It is a state of physical and mental well-being in which an individual’s body can accomplish duties and activities effectively and efficiently.
pg029_n0024: Fitness in sports can be categorised into physical and mental fitness.
pg029_n0025: For exercises to be a tool for body fitness, it must be performed well to avoid harming body parts and systems.
pg029_n0026: Therefore, a proper exercise must start by a warm up and end by a cool down.
pg030_n0005: Before and after every physical activity, an individual is required to do some simple activities for safety, which are warming up and cooling down, respectively.
pg030_n0009: Warm-up is crucial for the body before exercising or playing sport.
pg030_n0010: It prepares the body and mind for forthcoming activity.
pg030_n0015: Gradually raise the temperature of the body;
pg030_n0021: Increase the range of motion of the body joints.
pg030_n0027: General warm-up, that focuses to prepare the body systems via aerobic activities and mobility exercises;
pg030_n0030: Specific warm-up, that focuses on activity-related movements to prepare the muscle for the main activity; and
pg030_n0033: Stretching, this focuses on preparing the muscles and their associated tissues.
pg030_n0037: A warm-up should not leave an individual tired.
pg030_n0038: To carry out a proper warm-up one can do the following for at least 10 to 15 minutes:
pg030_n0042: Walk by increasing your speed for at least 3 minutes;
pg030_n0045: Jog slowly for at least 3 minutes;
pg030_n0048: Add some movements while jogging such as arm circling, knee ups, leg-back and heels kicking your buttocks alternately for at least 3 minutes;
pg030_n0051: Jog slowly and then walk for at least 3 minutes; and
pg030_n0054: Perform stretching exercises such as elbow and arm stretching for at least 3 minutes, as shown in Figure 3.1.
pg041_n0005: The performance related physical fitness comprises five key components, of which should be addressed to promote good performance in sports, namely agility, balance, coordination, reaction time and power.
pg041_n0009: Balance can be defined as the ability of an individual to maintain the line of gravity within the support base.
pg041_n0010: This includes static and dynamic balance.
pg041_n0011: Static balance is the ability to maintain balance in stationary position, while dynamic balance is the ability to maintain balance while moving.
pg041_n0012: Body balance is commonly measured by single leg stance test.
pg041_n0016: Exercises like balance beam walk, single leg balance, balance walk, single leg squat, single leg dead lift and leg swing can be used to improve the body balance.
pg041_n0018: The following is how to perform single leg stance:
pg041_n0022: Hold hands on the hip with eyes open;
pg041_n0025: Stand by one leg un-assisted for at least 10 seconds; and
pg041_n0028: Do the same with another leg.

pg044_n0016: The agility T-test is commonly used in measuring body agility.
pg044_n0020: Different drills can be used to improve agility, some of them are: T-drills, shuttle runs, high knee drills, ladder drills, hurdle drills, and cone drills.

pg063_n0003: Law number nine: Ball in and out of play
pg063_n0005: When the ball is inside the field of play and the referee has not yet halted play, the ball is in play.
pg063_n0006: When the ball, whether in the air or on the ground, completely crosses the sidelines or the goal lines, it is no longer in play.
pg063_n0007: The ball is still in play if it bounces off a goalpost, crossbar, corner flag post, the official, or one of the assistant officials and stays within the playing area.
pg063_n0009: Law number ten: Methods of scoring
pg063_n0011: If there are no further violations, a goal is scored when the ball completely crosses the goal line between the goalposts and under the crossbar.
pg063_n0012: The team that scores the most wins the game.
pg063_n0013: The game is deemed a draw if neither team scores more goals than the other, or if no goals are scored at all.
pg063_n0017: When a ball is passed forward, a player is considered offside, if he or she is in the opposing team’s half of the field; closer to the opposing team’s goal line than the ball; and there are no more than two defenders, including the goalkeeper, closer to the goal line than the attacking player.
pg063_n0018: Therefore, the attacking player between the ball and the last defender near the opposition’s goal line will be in the offside position.
pg063_n0019: When a player is flagged for being offside, the opposing team is given a free kick.
pg063_n0021: Law number twelve: Fouls and misconducts
pg063_n0023: A player has committed a foul if recklessly trips, kicks, pushes, or charges another player; strikes, tries to strike, or spits at them; makes a tackle but makes contact with the opponent before the ball; purposefully hands the ball, goalkeepers in their area exempted; or obstructs an opponent or prevents them from releasing the ball.
pg063_n0027: After a foul or other violations, the play is restarted with a free-kick, which is typically taken from the spot where the offence was committed.
pg063_n0028: Free kicks can be direct, where the taker scores immediately, or indirect, where a ball must first be touched by the taker and a second member of the same side.
pg063_n0032: When a defensive player fouls an attacking player within his or her penalty area, a penalty-kick is given.
pg063_n0033: The goalkeeper and penalty kicker are the only players allowed closer than nine point one five meters to the penalty spot when the kick is being taken.

pg066_n0020: Track events should be conducted with due observation on safety and the overall positive experience of all participants.
pg066_n0021: The following are some precautionary measures to consider in track events to ensure a well-being of athletes and running environment:
pg066_n0025: Proper warm-up and stretching: Athletes should engage in a thorough warm-up routine before their events to prepare their muscles for main activities.
pg066_n0026: Dynamic stretches and mobility exercises are particularly helpful for preventing runners from the risk of injuries;
pg067_n0005: Appropriate footwear: Athletes should wear proper athletic shoes designed for their specific events and track surfaces.
pg067_n0006: This helps to prevent slips, falls, and injuries;
pg067_n0009: Event-specific training: Athletes should receive proper training for their specific events to ensure proper form and reduce the risk of injuries;
pg067_n0012: Adequate rest and recovery: Athletes should get enough rest and recovery between practices and events to prevent overuse injuries and fatigue;
pg067_n0015: Hydration: Athletes should drink enough water before, during, and after their practices and events, especially in hot weather;
pg067_n0018: Event-specific equipment: Ensure that any equipment used in the events, such as starting blocks, hurdles, and batons are properly maintained in good condition;
pg067_n0021: Event specific rules and regulations: Athletes should be familiar with the rules and regulations of their events to avoid unnecessary accidents and disqualifications;
pg067_n0024: Know the track: Athletes should be familiar with the track layout, curves, and markings to anticipate their movements and reduce the risk of collisions;
pg067_n0027: Safe environment: The track and field area should be clear of debris, obstacles, or any hazardous material that can cause accidents; and

pg090_n0015: When running fifteen hundred meters, look straight ahead for at least thirty to forty meters to help to maintain speed and reduce shoulder and neck discomfort.

pg090_n0024: Avoid tightening the hands into fists when running; instead, keep them relaxed with the thumb resting on the top of the fingers.

pg090_n0030: Swing the hands forward and back in a straight manner and allow arms to cross in front of the chest.

pg090_n0035: Keep the back straight and lean slightly toward the middle of the foot as you are running; this will help to propel forward and land on the middle of the foot rather than the heel.
pg090_n0039: When running, avoid lifting the knees higher than the hips.
pg090_n0040: When the foot hits the ground, aim to land with a little bend in the knee to absorb some of the impact.

pg007_n0008_easy_read: Sport Studies play an important role in students’ physical, mental, and social development.
pg007_n0009_easy_read: In Sport Studies, students have chances to take part in different physical activities. These activities include sports and games for leisure and for competition.
pg007_n0010_easy_read: In this chapter, you will learn: the concept and elements of Sport Studies; the categories and functions of sports; the importance of studying Sport Studies; the relationship between Sport Studies and other subjects.
pg007_n0011_easy_read: The skills you develop will help you: understand the value of sports; build interest in taking part in different sports activities.
pg007_n0019_easy_read: In this book, Sport Studies means the same as Physical Education, P E.
pg007_n0020_easy_read: Sport Studies is the study of sports and the human movements linked to them.
pg007_n0021_easy_read: Sport Studies is an academic subject. It helps develop: thinking skills; movement skills; character; behavior. This development supports individual well-being and social change through physical activities and sports.
pg007_n0022_easy_read: Sport Studies aims to develop students’ physical competence, sport skills, knowledge of movement, and safety skills. It also helps students use these skills in many activities linked to sports and a healthy lifestyle.
pg007_n0023_easy_read: So, this subject is still an important part of education. It promotes active lifestyles. It also helps people take part in sports, exercise, and recreational activities throughout life during leisure time.
pg009_n0005_easy_read: Sport Studies uses different parts in school programs to reach its goal.
pg009_n0006_easy_read: Physical activity is the main part of Sport Studies.
pg009_n0010_easy_read: Physical activity is any body movement that uses energy.
pg009_n0011_easy_read: Any movement you do during the day is physical activity.
pg009_n0012_easy_read: Examples of physical activities are: cooking, taking a shower, walking, carrying chairs, and speaking.
pg009_n0013_easy_read: Physical activity includes sport-related activities and non-sport-related activities.
pg009_n0014_easy_read: In sport-related physical activities, the activities include: sports, exercise, dance, games, and play.
pg009_n0019_easy_read: Play can use the body and the mind. Play is often spontaneous and creative.
pg009_n0020_easy_read: Play activities may be planned or not planned. They can happen anywhere, such as open spaces, sandpits, and recreation rooms. They can start at any time.
pg009_n0021_easy_read: Sport Studies uses parts of play to make learning more enjoyable and more effective.
pg009_n0025_easy_read: Games are organized activities. They involve interaction and competition between the people who take part.
pg009_n0026_easy_read: Games can be played for fun or as part of a competitive sport.
pg009_n0027_easy_read: Games often have goals and rules for that situation. Players must follow the rules to reach the goals of the game.
pg009_n0028_easy_read: Games can be used in Sport Studies classes to help develop: skills, knowledge, character, and behavior.
pg009_n0032_easy_read: Sports are organized activities. They need physical effort and skill. In sports, one person or one team competes against another.
pg009_n0033_easy_read: Sports are a very organized, formal, and competitive type of play.
pg009_n0034_easy_read: Sports usually have official rules and regulations. People compete against each other, alone or in teams, to reach a goal, such as winning a game or a match.
pg009_n0035_easy_read: Examples of sports are: football, basketball, swimming, netball, and athletics, track and field events.
pg009_n0039_easy_read: Exercise is a planned, structured, and repeated body movement.
pg009_n0040_easy_read: Exercise is used to keep and improve physical fitness, improve health, and improve sport skills.
pg012_n0005_easy_read: Team sports are competitive physical activities. In team sports, people work together as a team to reach one common goal, as shown in Figure one point three.
pg012_n0006_easy_read: Examples include: football, netball, volleyball, field hockey, cricket, and a swimming relay.

pg012_n0012_easy_read: Sports have a positive effect on physical, psychological, cognitive, and emotional well-being. Sports also affect other parts of human life, including: social aspects, cultural aspects, political aspects, and economic aspects.

pg015_n0003_easy_read: Knowledge about body structure and body systems helps explain how the body works and how this affects sports performance. The same is true for knowledge and skills in: nutrition, health, and safety.
pg015_n0004_easy_read: Sports participants also support body health and fitness.
pg015_n0005_easy_read: So, when Sport Studies educators consider this relationship, they can adapt fitness programs for the best physical well-being and sports performance.
pg015_n0009_easy_read: Sport Studies and Physics have an important relationship because they both use knowledge about biomechanics and kinesiology.
pg015_n0010_easy_read: Sport Studies mainly focuses on: physical fitness, sports, and movement.
pg015_n0011_easy_read: This subject includes principles and laws about: motion, force, energy, density, floatation, and machines.
pg015_n0012_easy_read: Understanding the physics behind body movement and sports performance can improve learning and help athletes perform better.
pg015_n0016_easy_read: Sport Studies and Chemistry are connected through the study of biochemistry and nutrition.
pg015_n0017_easy_read: Chemistry is very important for studying the chemical processes that happen in the body during: exercise, metabolism, and energy production.
pg015_n0018_easy_read: Knowledge of Chemistry helps with: making diet recommendations, understanding how substances like supplements or drugs affect physical performance, and improving training programs for better results in Sport Studies.
pg015_n0022_easy_read: Sport Studies and Mathematics are connected in many parts of sports and exercise.
pg015_n0023_easy_read: Mathematics is used to study and understand data about: fitness levels, performance measures, and biomechanics.
pg015_n0024_easy_read: Also, mathematical ideas can help people understand: motion, trajectories, and the best training strategies. These ideas include: geometry, statistics, and calculus.
pg015_n0025_easy_read: Using Mathematics in Sport Studies can lead to: better-informed decisions, better training methods, and better overall physical performance.
pg015_n0029_easy_read: Sport Studies and Geography are connected in outdoor physical activities.
pg015_n0030_easy_read: Geographical knowledge, skills, and features affect the sports and recreational activities that participants choose.
pg015_n0031_easy_read: Understanding geographical factors is important for planning and organizing Sport Studies programs. These factors include: altitude, temperature, and landscapes.
pg015_n0032_easy_read: For example, some sports, such as orienteering, require understanding of: map reading, grid, weather, altitude, and wild life.
pg016_n0005_easy_read: The link between Sport Studies and History can be seen in how sports and physical activities change over time.
pg016_n0006_easy_read: Historical records show that sports and exercise have always been an important part of human civilizations. They have been used for: recreation, preparing for war, and cultural practices.
pg016_n0007_easy_read: Studying the history of different sports helps us understand: how sports developed, how different cultures affected physical activities, and how society viewed physical fitness and athletic skill in different time periods.
pg016_n0008_easy_read: Understanding this history can improve modern Sport Studies programs. It also shows why physical activities have been important in shaping societies over time.
pg016_n0012_easy_read: Sport Studies and Civic education are connected. They help promote values such as: teamwork, cooperation, and fair play.
pg016_n0013_easy_read: Sport Studies gives students a way to take part in sports and physical activities. This helps students build a sense of citizenship.
pg016_n0014_easy_read: Through Sport Studies, students learn important parts of good citizenship, such as: respect, sportsmanship, and inclusivity.
pg016_n0015_easy_read: Sport Studies can improve people's overall well-being. This can help create healthier and more active members of society. This is good for the civic health of the community.
pg016_n0019_easy_read: Sport Studies and Languages, both local and foreign, are related.
pg016_n0020_easy_read: Sport Studies improve communication and language learning. They do this by improving: thinking skills, concentration, interaction, and teamwork.
pg016_n0021_easy_read: Language skills can help students: follow instructions, follow game plans in sports, and work well with others during exercise or sports activities.
pg016_n0025_easy_read: There are several ways to see the connection between Music and Sport Studies.
pg016_n0026_easy_read: For example, adding music to Sport Studies lessons may improve the learning environment.
pg016_n0027_easy_read: Exercise programs that use music, such as aerobic dance, can make the activity more interesting. They can also encourage students to: move with rhythm, improve coordination, and build endurance.
pg016_n0028_easy_read: Music can also help set the mood for: warm-ups, cool-downs, and different training phases. This can affect the pace and excitement of the class.
pg016_n0029_easy_read: On the other hand, exercise and sports can improve music composition and performance. They can also stimulate a person's functions and performance.

pg018_n0008_easy_read: When you enter a sports field, a court, or a track, remember this: Safety is more than a precaution.
pg018_n0009_easy_read: Safety is the foundation for unforgettable sports experiences.
pg018_n0010_easy_read: In this chapter, you will learn: what safety means, why safety is important, what sports injuries are, what causes sports injuries, safety practices for participants' safety, and safety practices for successful performance.
pg018_n0011_easy_read: The competencies you develop will improve your ability to play different sports safely. They will also help you have a responsible attitude as an athlete.

pg018_n0019_easy_read: Safety is important in all physical exercise and sports. This is true in every part of the activity, at every age, and at every level of learning.
pg018_n0020_easy_read: Accidents and injuries can affect the good parts of sports and exercise.
pg018_n0021_easy_read: So, it is important for everyone to learn safety skills. These skills help prevent unnecessary injuries in physical activities and sports.
pg018_n0029_easy_read: Reduce the risk of injuries in physical activities;
pg018_n0032_easy_read: Develop the ability to manage injuries;
pg019_n0008_easy_read: Lower the risk of infection and disease;
pg019_n0011_easy_read: Increase comfort and reduce stress; and
pg019_n0014_easy_read: Build a positive image of sports in society.
pg019_n0018_easy_read: During exercise and sports, situations that can cause injuries are common.
pg019_n0019_easy_read: Injuries that happen right away during an event are called acute injuries. Injuries that develop slowly over many events are called overuse injuries.
pg019_n0020_easy_read: For example, if you fall and a piece of glass cuts you, the cut is an acute injury.
pg019_n0021_easy_read: If you play every day without enough rest, your knee may feel uncomfortable and start to swell. That is an overuse injury.
pg019_n0022_easy_read: So, all injuries are in two groups: acute injuries and overuse injuries.
pg019_n0024_easy_read: Different injuries can happen during exercise and sports. They can affect: muscles, joints, bones, and blood vessels.
pg019_n0025_easy_read: These injuries include: blisters, bruises, dislocation, sprain, fracture, strain, skin cuts, abrasions, muscle cramp, and nose bleeding.
pg019_n0029_easy_read: A blister is an injury. It happens when the skin rubs often. Then fluid fills a space between the layers of skin, as shown in Figure two point one.
pg019_n0030_easy_read: For example, foot blisters can happen when an athlete wears shoes that do not fit well.
pg019_n0031_easy_read: Holding a tennis or badminton racket for a long time may cause blisters on the hand.
pg019_n0032_easy_read: A blister that breaks is more likely to get infected. So, you must take care of it.

pg020_n0011_easy_read: Bruises are common sports injuries. They happen when a direct blow or a fall traps blood and makes it leak under the skin.
pg020_n0012_easy_read: The injured area may swell. A red or purple mark may appear on the skin, as shown in Figure two point two.
pg020_n0013_easy_read: Common symptoms of bruises include: pain and tenderness, swelling, warmth or heat, stiffness or limited movement, and itching while the bruise heals.

pg020_n0019_easy_read: A joint can become dislocated when force pushes the bones out of their normal position, as shown in Figure two point three.
pg020_n0020_easy_read: A dislocation is when bones slip out of place in a joint. This happens when strong force twists the ligament.
pg020_n0021_easy_read: Dislocation happens when the tissues around the joint, like tendons and ligaments, are damaged.
pg020_n0022_easy_read: Common symptoms of dislocation include: severe pain, deformity, swelling, limited movement, numbness or tingling, instability, difficulty using the affected limb, popping sounds, shock, and disorientation.
pg020_n0023_easy_read: This injury needs medical treatment to put the joint back in place.

pg021_n0009_easy_read: A sprain happens when a ligament stretches too much or tears. This happens when a joint is forced to move past its limit, as shown in Figure two point four.
pg021_n0010_easy_read: A sprain happens because of a sudden, unexpected twisting movement of the joint.
pg021_n0011_easy_read: This injury can be minor or very serious.
pg021_n0012_easy_read: If a ligament tears, it needs a lot of medical treatment.

pg022_n0005_easy_read: A fracture is a crack or break in a bone.
pg022_n0006_easy_read: If a fracture is open, it is called a compound fracture. If a fracture is closed, it is called a simple fracture. A simple fracture can be: displaced and non-displaced. Figure two point five shows this.
pg022_n0007_easy_read: The symptoms of a fracture may be different. They depend on the type of fracture and where it is.

- limited range of motion
- tenderness
- numbness or tingling
- crepitus
- shock
- disorientation

pg008_n0001: Sport Studies as a subject uses a number of terms. These terms include, movement, posture, performance, and healthy or active lifestyle.
pg008_n0003: Movement encompasses a broad range of skills that form the foundation for successful participation in games, sports and exercises. These skills can be categorised into locomotive, non-locomotive and manipulative. Locomotive skills include, walking, running, jumping and landing, hopping, leaping, sliding and dodging, while non-locomotive skills include, bending and stretching, twisting and turning, pushing and pulling as well as swinging and swaying. On the other hand manipulative skills include, throwing, catching, striking, dribbling, kicking and volleying.
pg008_n0005: Posture is the bodily positioning of a person during rest, standing or moving. Good posture entails a correct positioning and proper alignment that provide the individual with a comfortable sensation. Therefore, you have to execute a proper posture in every physical activity you do for safety and precise performance.
pg008_n0007: Performance is the use of physical and mental effort to produce effective outcomes when participating in physical activity. Performance in sports refers to the ability to demonstrate proficiency and skills in a particular sport.
pg008_n0009: A healthy or active-lifestyle refers to a way of living that promotes physical, mental, and emotional well-being of an individual through regular participation in physical activities, eating balanced diet, and positive lifestyle choices. It encompasses a variety of habits and behaviours that contribute to overall health and wellbeing. Healthy movements may include walking, sporting, dancing, yoga and running. For a healthy living, active life should be coupled with eating a well-balanced diet. The emphasis is on encouraging consuption of low-fat diet with plenty of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.

pg061_n0008: One of the characteristics of sports is the presence of a global governing body of the particular sport. The Federation of International Football Association (FIFA) is the world football governing body. To ensure that the game is played safely and fairly, FIFA enacted 17 laws which are briefly explained in this section:
pg061_n0009: Law no.1: The field of play
pg061_n0010: The game must be played in a marked rectangular field of between 90-120 m in length and 45-90 m width.
pg061_n0012: The ball must be made of approved materials with a diameter of 68.5 – 71 cm, a weight between 410 – 450 g and pressure of between 0.6 – 1.1 atmospheres at sea level.
pg061_n0014: A football match consists of two teams and each team has a maximum of 11 players including a goalkeeper. During a break in play, an outfield player may switch places with the goalkeeper. A football match cannot start or continue without at least seven players on each team. Since 2021, it has become mandatory that each team may substitute a maximum of 5 players instead of 3 players during an official competition.
pg062_n0002: In football match, a T-shirt, shorts, stockings, shin guards, and football boots are the required items for players involved. Only goalkeepers are required to wear a uniform that differentiates them from other members of their team, rival teams, and referees. Head gear may be used provided it does not endanger other players. The majority of jewellery is prohibited.
pg062_n0004: The referee is the final arbiter and interpreter of the football rules in the game of football. The referee makes the call on whether a game to continue or not, and he has the authority to stop play if a player needs medical attention. He or she issues warnings (verbal or yellow cards), and expulsions (red cards), and is in charge of keeping track of time, keeping records, and making sure that all match gear and clothes are in order.
pg062_n0006: The assistant referees, formerly called linesmen. They primarily support the referee by signaling for corner kicks, throw-ins, and offside infringements. They must also bring the referee’s attention to any other fouls or infringements that the referee may not have seen when committed. However, the referee’s decision is always final.
pg062_n0007: Law no.7: Duration of the match
pg062_n0008: A football match consists of 90 minutes with two halves of 45 minutes of play, and additional time may be added at the referee’s discretion in case of injuries, substitutions, and time wasting, as well as time can be added to allow a penalty to be taken after normal time. pg062_n0010: The game begins with a tossing coin. The winners of a toss select the first half’s ends, while the loser’s kick-off. The restart of the game occurs during the start of the second half where the opposing team begins to play. The game can also restart each time the team score a goal. The centre point is used for the kick-off, and the ball must be moved into the half of the opponent. The opposition must be at least 9.15 m from the ball, and all players must be inside their half of the field. Before the first player may touch the ball again, a second player must touch it.

pg075_n0013: Relay race is a track event in which athletes run in teams of four runners each. Each runner of a team runs a section or a leg of race in a track while exchanging baton in a specified zone. The team whose fourth runner finishes first, wins a race. Relay involves four phases, namely starting, running, baton exchange and finishing. Within each phase, there are various skills to be performed by participants. The most common relay races are the 4x100 m and 4x 400 m. Relays require equipment such as baton, pistol or clappers, flags and stopwatch.
pg075_n0015: (a) Baton should be exchanged in the exchanging zones and not otherwise; (b) Do not pass the baton by throwing to the outgoing runner; and

pg076_n0002: In 4x100 m relay, the first runner in a team is required to cover a 100 m distance while holding a baton before passing it to the second runner. The second runner will also cover a 100 m distance, the same to the third runner, as well as the fourth runner and completes the race. The 4x100 m requires an athlete to sprint at top speed throughout the race. The non-visual baton exchange is commonly used in this race.
pg076_n0003: The 4x100 m relay has three change-over zones, each one is 20 m in length. Prior to each change over zone is a 10 m acceleration zone. The sprinters usually place check mark on a precise distance from the start of acceleration zone. In this event, an athlete should be well positioned, have good reaction time at take-off stage and good baton exchanger, as well as good finisher in the finishing stage.

pg088_n0007: (a) In the first 200 m, you should get out with a good pace and avoid going to the inner lane immediately when comes off the first curve. The runner should also aim to start the next curve while running in straight line;

pg088_n0009: (c) From 400 to 600 m, consciously picks up the pace, runs fast and smoothly; and

pg088_n0011: Techniques to be developed for better performance include action of the head, shoulder, body, arms, leading leg and back leg.
pg088_n0013: The head should be kept still to avoid tightening the neck and shoulder muscles. The eyes should look at the ground at least 10 m in front of the athlete; the mouth should be slightly open to improve inhaling and increase the generation of energy in the muscles to keep on running over the required distance.
pg088_n0015: The arms should be held at an angle of approximately greater than ninety degrees and moved beneath the shoulders from the front to the rear and keep on swinging to drive forward and help to cover a longer distance with maximum energy and speed.
pg089_n0002: The leading knee is lifted straight up until the thigh is just below. This gives the stability when landing and controlling the whole body, hence relaxing muscles before taking the next stride. A perfect execution helps to run for a long time without undue fatigue.
pg089_n0004: The back leg must be in an extended position before it leaves the ground. This gives the body balance and stability when running. The leg muscles contract and generate energy for lifting the body weight and supporting a runner to keep on running.
